Definition: time, especially (adverb with preposition) now, when, etc.
BiblicalUsage: ʻÊth is time — the season, the moment, the appointed hour. To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under heaven; the psalmist commits his times into God's hand. It is the word for the shape of a life lived under God's timing.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe ʻêth is a word for trust: my times are in His hand, not mine, and His timing is never late. I hold that knowing there is a time for everything frees me from trying to make everything happen now.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
